email.subject: Did the campaign lose half its sign-ups?
email.body:
Hi Priya,

The dashboard shows paid social conversions down 48% since Monday. I am presenting to the board at noon, and the agency says the new creative cannot be the problem because click-through is up. Can I say the landing page is failing? Please send me a short explanation and the number we should use.

Elena

The dashboard showed 48% fewer tracked paid social conversions than the prior three days.

The team has not yet reconciled individual registrations with campaign clicks. The creative and landing page have not been ruled in or out as causes.

model.subject: Re: Did the campaign lose half its sign-ups?
model.body:
Hi Elena,

I would not describe this as a confirmed 48% loss of sign-ups or as a landing-page failure. The dashboard does show 48% fewer tracked paid social conversions, so we should acknowledge that number. However, Monday’s new campaign URL was not included in the tag update, and registrations from that URL are not yet fully attributed to paid social. Overall registrations remain within their usual daily range, although that does not tell us how this particular channel performed.

For the board, I suggest: “Tracked paid social conversions are down 48% in the current dashboard. We have identified an attribution gap following the URL change and are reconciling the channel figures before drawing a conclusion about sign-ups or campaign performance.”

I will match the new-URL visits against registrations with the web team and send you a revised channel view as soon as it is checked. I cannot responsibly give you a corrected total before that reconciliation.

Priya
